comment: This book is built by AI to describe distinct families and castles that share the name Rosenberg or its variations. Keep it concise and brief. Include information about each family, its members, and places related to it. Describe castles named Rosenberg in a separate section. Do not give detailed accounts of events or histories of specific people. Estates and Notable people keep simple. Dates in [YYYY] or [YYYY-YYYY] format

entries.title: Grabner, Lower Austria
entries.label: Grabner
entries.english: A Lower Austrian branch of the Lords of Graben, called Grabner zu Rosenberg from 1487 and Grabner zu Rosenburg by the late 16th century. The biographies describe the early family as modest lower nobility; Christoph Grabner expanded and consolidated its estates, establishing the house’s wealth. His son Sebastian I inherited his estates, and his grandson Georg became one of the family’s leading landholders, jointly holding Pottenbrunn with his half-brother Josaphat from 1535 to 1562, as the Grabner rose to prominence among Protestant nobles in the 16th century. The claimed descent from the Lords of Graben is presented by the biographers as probable, not certain.

entries.label: Brandenburg

img.name: Coat of arms of the von Bredow

entries.english: Recorded: [1338-1582]

Regional Brandenburg–Magdeburg Rosenberg bearers appear at Altenplathow (Plate), Schollene, Plaue, Kützkow, and Möckern. In 1338 Hans von Rosenberg and the brothers Wernher and Werenher were named in a protection agreement at Plate alongside men of Bredow. In 1405 Jan Rosenberg received the Möckern fiefs of his deceased brother Werner. Later records place Kützkow in Rosenberg hands in 1442 and 1550–1582, and a quarter of Stegelitz with the Rosenbergs of Kützkow in 1550–1554. Continuity from the 14th-century bearers and any connection to the Czech Rožmberks remain unestablished.

entries.title: Rosenberg, Aachen
entries.label: Aachen
entries.english: Recorded: [1362-1381]

A small Rosenberg family group is attested in two charters of Aachen’s court concerning property near Vetzauwen/Wetzschauwen and Burtscheid Abbey. In 1362, Nicolaus von Rosenberg is identified as the brother of Geirrart van Steinstroissen; both he and Willem, a son of Geirrart’s brother, served as sureties in Geirrart’s sale of his farm to Burtscheid Abbey. A 1381 charter records Nicolaus (there named Cloys) selling seven morgen of land near Wetzschauwen to the abbey. The documents do not establish the family’s origin or whether the Nicolaus named in both is certainly the same man.

entries.title: Rossberg / Schenkenschloss, Würzburg
label: Schenk
entries.english: Castle on the Roßberg above the Dürrbach valley, northwest of Würzburg, and ancestral seat of the Schenk von Roßberg (also called Schenk von Rossenberg), ministeriales of the bishopric who held the court office of cupbearer. The castle, first documented with its chapel in 1293, was called Roßberg until about 1600. A fire damaged it in 1445; it was rebuilt and enlarged in 1448. The Peasants’ War rebels burned it in 1525. Georg Schenk von Roßberg, unable to rebuild, surrendered the fief to the bishopric in 1537. The ruin was later quarried; the restored keep is the principal surviving structure.

entries.title: Gut Rosenberg, Horbach (Aachen), Germany
label: Aachen
entries.english: Historic fortified-style farmstead, rather than a castle, in Horbach north-west of Aachen. First documented on 26 May 1274, when the knight Johannes de Porcheto acquired it; it was a fief of the archbishop of Cologne and from 1361 lay within the Jülich lordship of Heyden. The four-sided farmyard was formerly almost surrounded by water. The present complex incorporates older fabric, with the main portal dated 1784, a former barn dated 1825, and a stable bearing 1914 anchors. The estate name’s origin is unknown. Restored, it has housed the Aachen Chamber of Crafts’ Academy for Craft Design since 1994. [History](https://www.gut-rosenberg.de/downloads/akademie-fuer-handwerksdesign-geschichte-gutshof-gut-rosenberg-6332%2C632.pdf) · [Academy](https://www.gut-rosenberg.de/artikel/gut-rosenberg-6332%2C471%2C1186.html)

entries.title: Rosenberg Castle (Rosenburg am Kamp), Lower Austria
entries.english: Castle above the Kamp at the Taffa confluence in the Kamptal, near Horn; it was called Rosenberg until the 16th century. The local ministerial family is documented from 1175 to 1290. In 1290 Hartlieb von Rosenberg witnessed a charter at Altenburg; his low standing in the witness list has been taken to suggest that his family may already have lost the castle. In 1345 a charter was issued at Schloss Rosenberch in which Wulfing von Stallegg renounced certain revenues, showing the castle remained in use under the Stalleggers. In 1433, after a dispute with Jörg Grünpeck, Duke Albrecht V awarded Rosenburg to Wolfgang von Winden; the castle was reportedly occupied and damaged by Hussite forces that year. Johann von Winden owned it in 1467. Kaspar von Rogendorf acquired it around 1475–1478, and the Rogendorfs expanded the castle and built its late Gothic chapel, probably consecrated in 1484. That year the Abbot of Altenburg reportedly brought the monastery’s valuables there for safekeeping. In 1486 the Rogendorfs made substantial payments to King Matthias Corvinus to avert devastation and plundering. The Grabner brothers acquired the castle in 1487 and made the estate a major Protestant center in Lower Austria. Sebastian Grabner transformed the medieval fortress into a Renaissance palace in 1593–1597. After changing hands in the 17th century, the Hoyos family acquired the castle and lordship in 1681. Fires and neglect caused partial decay; restoration between 1859 and 1889 gave the complex much of its present character. [Local chronicle](https://www.rosenburg-mold.at/Chronik_Rosenburg) · [EBIDAT castle database](https://www.ms-visucom.de/cgi-bin/ebidat.pl?id=1928) · [Burgen-Austria history](https://www.burgen-austria.com/archive.php?id=375)

entries.title: Burgruine Rosenberg, Berneck, Switzerland
entries.english: Ruins of a hill castle above Berneck, also called Bernang-Rosenberg. First recorded in 1210, it passed from the Lords of Bernang through the monastery of St Gallen to the Lords of Rosenberg; the castle buildings were sold for demolition in 1811.
label: Rorschach

entries.title: Rosenburg (Klein Rosenburg), Barby, Saxony-Anhalt
label: Brandenburg
entries.english: Castle site on the Saale floodplain near its confluence with the Elbe. The royal estate is recorded in 965 and a castle in 1269; the Counts of Barby held it as a Magdeburg fief from 1306/08. It served as a Barby family residence until 1330 and again from 1595 to 1614. The residence was rebuilt in the 16th century; surviving remains include the gate tower, parts of the enclosure, and vaulted cellars.

entries.title: Rosenburg, Sulzbach-Rosenberg, Bavaria
label: Sulzbach
entries.english: Vanished hilltop castle on the Schlossberg above Rosenberg in the Upper Palatinate. Probably built around 1100, Duke Friedrich pledged it to the Fronberg brothers in 1386; it became the Hofmark Rosenberg in 1410 and declined from the 16th century. The keep stump is incorporated into the town war memorial.

entries.title: Ruine Rosenberg, Rügland, Bavaria
entries.english: Hilltop castle ruin above the village of Rosenberg, once held by the Lords of Vestenberg zu Rosenberg. The site retains earthworks, a moat, and a two-storey corner tower of sandstone.

entries.title: Rosenburg, Riedenburg, Bavaria
entries.english: Castle on a ridge above Riedenburg in the Altmühltal, probably built in the mid-12th century and transferred to Duke Ludwig I of Bavaria in 1196. It retains a Romanesque core with later Renaissance buildings and now houses a hunting museum and falconry centre.

entries.title: Rožmberk Castle (Rosenberg), South Bohemia
label: Czechia
entries.english: Castle above the Vltava founded by Vok I of Rosenberg around the mid-13th century and documented in 1250. The Upper Castle was largely destroyed by fire in 1522; the Lower Castle was rebuilt in Renaissance style and later remodelled by the Buquoy family.

entries.title: Festung Rosenberg, Kronach, Bavaria
entries.english: Bamberg episcopal stronghold first recorded in 1249. Medieval and early modern fortifications gave it a pentagonal form by 1699; the town acquired the fortress in 1888, and it now houses the Franconian Gallery.

entries.title: Schloss Rosenberg, Rosenberg (Buchen), Baden-Württemberg
label: Franken
Mönch
entries.english: Vanished castle at Schlossplatz in Rosenberg, now part of Buchen. The Mönch von Rosenberg held it in 1251, followed from the late 13th century by the Lords of Rosenberg. After the line ended in 1632, the estate passed to other noble houses; the last above-ground remains disappeared in 1926.

entries.title: Rosenbach, Haslach, Bolzano, South Tyrol
label: Triest
entries.english: The Rosenbach family is attested among the ministeriales of the bishops of Trent at Sibidat, a vanished settlement in Haslach below Weineck, in 1178. The location of a castle called Rosenbach is unknown. An older study proposed that the family was a branch of the Lords of Weineck and placed their castle below Weineck, near the present Holy Sepulchre Church, but this location is not confirmed; a later study explicitly notes that Rosenbach's location is unknown and that the records may refer to two families.
